subject: amplification of rounding errors and the constrained space

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: amplification of rounding errors and the constrained space
parts:
Hi!

I was wondering if the automatic unconstraining transformations take amplification of rounding errors into account or if I don't need to worry about this.

So the problem I see is that whenever I declare a parameter to be positive, it is actually being sampled on the log space as far as I am aware. In my Stan program I get the exponential of it. Now, the gradients are being calculated wrt to the positive value and via the chain rule things are put back together. What worries me is that some functions which I use with the positive numbers are potentially not numerically very exact (e.g. ODEs is a classic example). Can this lead to an uncontrolled amplification of the rounding errors which makes the gradients in-exact?

In short: Is it beneficial to calculate straight on the unconstrained space whenever numerically less accurate functions are involved? So instead of modeling with (positive) rate constants, I should really work only with the logs of these and don't rely on automatic constraining and unconstraining. The price to pay then is that I have tons of exp expression in my code...

Anyone having some experience with this?

Thanks much.

Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] amplification of rounding errors and the constrained space
parts:
The issue with exp() is overflow (and conversely, rounding down to zero), not rounding.

You want to make sure that you don't wind up with gradients that are too crazy, but everything's on the log scale, so the Jacobian's not too bad (just x from log |d/dx exp(x)|).

- Bob
